Provides test cases for a static analysis linter that detects `map[K]bool` values used as sets rather than genuine boolean maps, covering both positive (should-flag) and negative (should-not-flag) scenarios.

## Key Components

| Function / Variable | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `setWithMake` | ✅ Flag | Declares a `map[string]bool` via `make` with only `true` assignments |
| `setWithCompositeLiteral` | ✅ Flag | Composite literal map with all-`true` values |
| `setWithIntKey` | ✅ Flag | Non-string key type (`int`) still detected as a set |
| `setReInitWithMake` | ✅ Flag | Map re-initialized with `make`; all assignments remain `true` |
| `setUsedInClosure` | ✅ Flag | Set pattern holds even when assigned inside a closure |
| `setVarDecl` | ✅ Flag | `var` declaration followed by `make` and `true`-only writes |
| `packageLevelSet` | ✅ Flag | Package-level unexported composite literal, all values `true` |
| `genuineBoolMap` | ❌ Skip | Assigns both `true` and `false`, so it is a real boolean map |
| `boolMapFromCompositeLiteral` | ❌ Skip | Composite literal contains a `false` value |
| `boolMapFromCompositeLiteralWithChange` | ❌ Skip | A key is later set to `false` after initialization |
| `boolMapFromFunctionCall` | ❌ Skip | Sourced from a function return — provenance is unknown |
| `boolMapReassignedFromFunc` | ❌ Skip | Reassigned from a function, tainting the variable |
| `boolMapParameter` | ❌ Skip | Passed in as a parameter; caller context unknown |
| `boolMapCopied` | ❌ Skip | Map aliased to another variable, escapes local tracking |
| `noIndexedAssignments` | ❌ Skip | Only read access (`m["a"]`), no write assignments |
| `boolMapFromRangeValue` | ❌ Skip | Map value extracted from a range over a nested map |
| `boolMapAssignedVariable` | ❌ Skip | Assignment uses a variable (`val`) rather than literal `true` |
| `ExportedMap` | ❌ Skip | Exported package-level identifiers are excluded from the lint rule |
| `boolMapPassedToFunc` | ❌ Skip | Map passed to another function, escapes local scope |
| `multiReturnVar` | ❌ Skip | Both variables come from a multi-return call, both tainted |

## Usage Example

```go
// Run the linter against this file to validate detection logic:
// (from the analyzer's test harness)

analysistest.Run(t, testdata, analyzer, "example")
```

The `// want` comments act as inline assertions for [`go/analysis`](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/analysistest) — each flagged line must produce a diagnostic matching the quoted pattern (e.g., `` `map\[string\]bool used as a set` ``), while lines without `// want` must produce no diagnostic.

## Notes

- **Escape heuristics:** The linter suppresses warnings when a map variable *escapes* — passed to a function, aliased, or sourced from a non-literal — to avoid false positives.
- **Exported symbols** at the package level are always skipped.
- **Multi-return assignments** taint all assigned variables simultaneously.
